A1.justification: Both complete 23-page PDFs describe the same work. Scientific text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.12 match. Pages 2–23 have identical extracted text and rendered images; differences are confined to first-page publication and version notices.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments evaluating dropout and opacity noise on LLFF, DTU, and Blender in Tables 1–2, plus ablations and supplementary empirical analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark experiments, ablations, qualitative comparisons, and supplementary results reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical CA computation, random Gaussian dropout, inference-time opacity scaling, and multiplicative opacity noise. No algorithm or component changes appear in the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same LLFF, DTU, and Blender data and sparse-view synthesis tasks. Supplementary depth reconstruction and multi-view learning scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains 3DGS, DNGaussian, FSGS, CoR-GS, and Binocular3DGS; Table 2 retains 3DGS, DNGaussian, and Binocular3DGS. Supplementary comparison methods, including AbsGS and alternative dropout strategies, are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains three training views for LLFF and DTU, eight for Blender, and identical downsampling, evaluation metrics, and CA computation settings. The supplementary evaluation protocols also match.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendices A.2–A.10 retain the same qualitative comparisons, dropout and noise ablations, SH analyses, Gaussian-count analysis, geometry evaluation, and multi-view experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent experimental run counts, seed specifications, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The stochastic rendering and variance-estimation procedures are identical.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–15 and all plotted and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports LLFF Binocular3DGS PSNR of 21.44 for the baseline and 22.12 with dropout in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations are identical, including the CA definition, Appendix A.1's dropout-variance derivation, Appendix A.6's color-variance definition, and Appendix A.9's Concrete Dropout formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about co-adaptation causing appearance artifacts, the CA metric, increased view density reducing co-adaptation, and the benefits of dropout and opacity noise.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations are identical. Appendix A.12 retains the limitation that excessive co-adaptation suppression can reduce rendering quality and representational capacity.

D1.justification: Sections 4.1 and A.11 retain the same implementation disclosures, including dropout probability 0.2, opacity-noise tuning within [0.05, 0.8], unified scene settings, and white-background retraining. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 60 references are unchanged, including the positioning relative to DropoutGS and DropGaussian. The updated publication notice does not revise the scientific positioning.

P1.justification: The first-page footer changes from 'Preprint. Under review.' to the NeurIPS 2025 conference notice. The arXiv stamp changes from v1, 18 Aug 2025, to v3, 20 Sep 2025. All body language and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–14 and Tables 1–15 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. Page layout is unchanged; the first-page differences only update publication and version text.

improvement.justification: v3 only updates the publication notice and arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific content, empirical evidence, theoretical analysis, limitations, and reproducibility information remain identical, including the appendices. These metadata edits establish no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
